records.label: Indian family with two affected siblings

variants.as_reported: novel homozygous truncating mutation in the Neuroblastoma-Amplified Sequence (NBAS) gene

quotes: We analyzed an Indian family with two affected siblings by exome sequencing and identified a novel homozygous truncating mutation in the Neuroblastoma-Amplified Sequence (NBAS) gene in the patients' genome.
Acrofrontofacionasal Dysostosis type 1 (AFFND1) is an extremely rare, autosomal recessive syndrome, comprising facial and skeletal abnormalities, short stature and intellectual disability.

notes.statement: Palagano et al. (2018) described acrofrontofacionasal dysostosis type 1 as an extremely rare autosomal recessive syndrome comprising facial and skeletal abnormalities, short stature, and intellectual disability.
quotes: Acrofrontofacionasal Dysostosis type 1 (AFFND1) is an extremely rare, autosomal recessive syndrome, comprising facial and skeletal abnormalities, short stature and intellectual disability.

notes.statement: Palagano et al. (2018) found that overexpression of the truncated NBAS protein in HEK293T cells impaired both nonsense-mediated decay and Golgi-to-endoplasmic reticulum retrograde traffic, as assessed by real-time PCR, Western blot, coimmunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence.
quotes: Both functions were impaired in HEK293T cells overexpressing the truncated NBAS protein, as assessed by Real-Time PCR, Western blot analysis, co-immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence analysis.

notes.statement: By immunohistochemistry in mouse embryos at various developmental stages, Palagano et al. (2018) detected NBAS expression in developing chondrogenic and osteogenic structures of the skeleton and in the cortex, hippocampus, and cerebellum, compatible with a role in bone and brain development.
quotes: detected expression in developing chondrogenic and osteogenic structures of the skeleton as well as in the cortex, hippocampus and cerebellum, which is compatible with a role in bone and brain development

notes.statement: Palagano et al. (2018) found that depletion of endogenous nbas in zebrafish embryos resulted in defective morphogenesis of chondrogenic cranial skeletal elements, pointing to a conserved function of NBAS in skeletal morphogenesis.
quotes: Functional genetics in the zebrafish model showed that depletion of endogenous z-nbas in fish embryos results in defective morphogenesis of chondrogenic cranial skeletal elements.
